units.title: The handbook uses interstate to mean a controlled-access highway with multiple lanes.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Before entering an interstate, identify a gap in the nearest traffic lane.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: At an entrance ramp, wait for the broken-white-line portion, then adjust speed, signal and merge into a safe gap.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: On the interstate, maintain a steady traffic-compatible speed while obeying posted limits.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Keep slower traffic right and avoid unnecessary lane changes; ordinarily remain right unless overtaking.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Watch entrance ramps and, if safe, signal and move left to help entering traffic merge.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Signal before changing lanes and check blind spots before passing.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: After missing an interstate exit, continue to the next exit rather than backing up or using an emergency crossover.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Do not cross an interstate median.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual lists forty miles per hour as the interstate minimum speed.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Plan an exit early, signal and reach its proper lane at least a mile before the intended exit.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: For an interstate exit, slow after entering the deceleration lane and check the ramp's advised speed.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: After leaving the interstate, watch for two-way traffic and newly posted speed limits.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Use headlights between sunset and sunrise.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can see the vehicle; parking lamps alone are unlawful for driving.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Switch off auxiliary driving lamps when approaching from ahead or behind at the same time headlights require dimming.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Choose a night-driving speed that permits stopping within the illuminated roadway.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Use high beams on open highways, but dim them for oncoming vehicles and when following within two hundred feet.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: If oncoming glare is blinding, look toward the right road edge instead of directly at the lights.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Keep both sides of the windshield clean and move your gaze instead of staring into the headlight-lit spot.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: In rain, slow to match surface conditions; hydroplaning occurs when the tires ride on water instead of contacting the road.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Rain may require disengaging cruise control; use low beams and increase the following gap.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Do not enter a flooded roadway; turn around and find another route.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Floodwater can conceal dips or a damaged road surface even when it appears shallow.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual warns that six inches of water can reach the underside of most passenger cars and cause stalling or lost control.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual warns that two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including SUVs and pickups.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: If no alternate route exists around flooding, go to higher ground and wait for the water to recede; use extra caution at night.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: In fog, use low beams, reduce speed and proceed with extreme caution.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual advises against travel on roads posted at forty miles per hour or more when visibility is below a quarter mile.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Small and high-profile vehicles are especially affected by wind; anticipate corrections after leaving shelter or meeting large vehicles.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Watch for high-wind advisories while travelling.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: On snow or ice, slow down, increase following distance, clear the windows and make speed or direction changes gradually.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: For snowy or icy conditions, the handbook tells non-ABS drivers to pump the brake pedal to avoid lockup; rolling tires are needed for steering.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: For snowy or icy conditions with ABS, press firmly and do not pump the brakes.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: On a slippery uphill climb, apply enough power to maintain speed without spinning the wheels.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The printed studded-tire season runs from November first to April first.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual advises against driving in blizzards because poor visibility, slippery surfaces and wind occur together.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: If stranded in a blizzard, stay calm and remain with the vehicle.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: For a stranded vehicle, crack a window for ventilation and use the engine and heater sparingly only with ventilation and a snow-free exhaust pipe.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Use hazard flashers to help work crews see a stranded vehicle and use its interior lamp at night.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: If several people are stranded together, alternate sleeping and keeping watch.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: If wheels drop off pavement, grip the steering wheel firmly and straddle the edge instead of immediately turning back.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: After an edge drop, reduce speed, check traffic and return gradually to the driving lane when safe.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Visual distraction takes the eyes away, manual distraction takes the hands away and cognitive distraction takes attention away from driving.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Text messaging can involve visual, manual and cognitive distraction together.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The handbook lists a texting-and-driving fine range of two hundred to five hundred dollars.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: A hands-free phone conversation can still distract the driver.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Eating, reading, handling clothing, reaching to the floor, grooming or changing media can distract a driver.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Children, other passengers and pets can distract the driver.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Secure children properly, keep them occupied appropriately and pull over safely if they need attention rather than tending to them while moving.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Keep passenger behavior under control and reserve arguments or upsetting conversations for a safe place outside the driving task.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Secure pets in an appropriate carrier, kennel or harness and do not allow a pet on the driver's lap.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Entering navigation destinations, searching for radio content or adjusting climate controls can distract from vehicle control.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Using portable-device internet or email while driving adds distraction and crash risk.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Set the seat, mirrors, climate and radio controls before beginning to drive.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Check messages before driving and ask passengers to operate navigation, radio or climate controls when help is needed.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual suggests using normal stops for vehicle-control adjustments.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The printed noncommercial rule prohibits handheld wireless use to read, type or send written messages while operating a motor vehicle.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual prohibits operating a vehicle on a public road with a television screen visible to the driver.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Watching crash scenes, police stops, construction, advertising, scenery or address details can draw attention away from driving.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Aggressive driving includes frightening or rude behavior such as tailgating, cutting off vehicles, running red lights or failing to yield.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Avoid driving while angry or upset and treat other road users courteously.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Begin a trip rested; if drowsy, stop driving and pull over safely for rest.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The handbook describes a short ten-to-twenty-minute nap as a fatigue-rest option.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The fatigue tips suggest a midafternoon break and avoiding early-morning or late-night driving.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Fatigue warnings include heavy eyelids, yawning, head nodding, missed signs, poor memory of recent miles and unintended lane departures.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The handbook mentions changing drivers as one response to fatigue.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The manual says an open window, chewing gum or loud radio does not prevent drowsiness and that caffeine or energy drinks are unreliable for alertness.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Do not use phone calls or texting as a way to stay awake while driving.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Defensive driving means staying alert to prevent crashes.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The handbook describes a look-ahead planning interval of at least ten to fifteen seconds.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Look to both sides where road users could cross, and check both directions at an intersection even after the signal changes.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Check rear traffic at least every ten seconds and when changing lanes, backing, slowing or descending steep hills.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: A shoulder glance checks the blind area beside the vehicle that mirrors do not show.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Signal at least one hundred feet before a planned direction change, including lane changes, turns, freeway entry or leaving a curb.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Use headlights when other vehicles are hard to see and whenever the windshield wipers are used.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: A sharp horn blast can warn of an immediate collision danger; brief brake taps can warn following drivers of slowing.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Maintain a space cushion around the vehicle to allow time to react, stop or pass safely.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: To check following space, time the gap from a fixed roadside marker; reaching it in less than three seconds is too close, and adversity calls for a longer gap.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: The handbook treats three seconds as a following-distance minimum and adds one second for each adverse factor, such as rain or heavy traffic.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving

units.title: Keep lateral space from oncoming traffic and parked vehicles, and protect rear space through steady speed and advance slowing signals.
units.domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
units.readiness_domain: Interstates, weather, distraction and defensive driving
